mcqs.question: Which of the following reactions is a double displacement (metathesis) reaction?
mcqs.explanation: In a double displacement reaction, the cations and anions of two compounds exchange partners. Option B shows Na⁺ swapping with Ag⁺, forming NaNO₃ and AgCl, which is a classic double displacement reaction. Option A is a single displacement (metal replaces another metal). Option C is a combination reaction, and Option D is a decomposition reaction.

mcqs.question: In which of the following reactions will a solid precipitate be formed?
mcqs.explanation: BaSO₄ is insoluble in water, so when BaCl₂ and Na₂SO₄ are mixed a white precipitate of BaSO₄ forms. Options A, C, and D either involve only soluble ions or produce a gas, not a precipitate.

mcqs.question: Which equation represents a single displacement (replacement) reaction?
mcqs.explanation: In a single displacement reaction, a more reactive element (Fe) displaces a less reactive element (Cu) from its compound. Options B, C, and D are combination, dissociation, and decomposition reactions respectively.

mcqs.question: If a metal X can displace copper from CuSO₄ solution, which statement about X is correct?

options.A: X is less reactive than copper.
options.B: X is more reactive than copper.
options.C: X has the same reactivity as copper.
options.D: Reactivity cannot be inferred from this observation.

mcqs.answer: X is more reactive than copper.
mcqs.explanation: A metal can displace another metal from its compound only if it is higher in the reactivity series. Hence X must be more reactive than copper. The other options contradict the principle of displacement reactions.

mcqs.learning_point: Use metal reactivity to predict displacement
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a single displacement reaction from a double displacement reaction?

options.A: In single displacement, two compounds exchange ions; in double displacement, an element replaces another.
options.B: In single displacement, an element replaces another element in a compound; in double displacement, the cations and anions of two compounds exchange.
options.C: Both reactions involve exchange of cations only.
options.D: Both reactions always produce a precipitate.

mcqs.answer: In single displacement, an element replaces another element in a compound; in double displacement, the cations and anions of two compounds exchange.
mcqs.explanation: A single displacement (replacement) reaction involves a free element displacing another element from its compound. A double displacement (metathesis) reaction involves the exchange of ions between two compounds. Options A, C, and D misstate the definitions.

mcqs.question: Which reaction can be used to remove hardness caused by Ca²⁺ ions in water?
mcqs.explanation: The reaction between calcium chloride and sodium carbonate is a double displacement reaction that forms insoluble calcium carbonate, which precipitates and removes Ca²⁺ hardness. Options B and C are single displacement reactions, and D is a combustion reaction.

mcqs.question: When aqueous solutions of lead(II) nitrate and potassium iodide are mixed, a yellow solid appears. Which compound is the precipitate?
mcqs.explanation: Pb²⁺ ions combine with I⁻ ions to form lead(II) iodide, PbI₂, which is insoluble and appears as a yellow precipitate. KNO₃ remains soluble, and the other options are reactants, not products of the precipitation.

mcqs.question: A student adds a piece of zinc metal to a solution of copper(II) sulfate. Which observation confirms that a displacement reaction has occurred?

options.A: The solution turns blue, zinc dissolves, and copper metal plates out on the zinc.
options.D: The temperature of the solution rises slightly without any other change.

mcqs.answer: The solution turns blue, zinc dissolves, and copper metal plates out on the zinc.
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from CuSO₄, forming ZnSO₄ (solution remains blue) and depositing copper metal. This is the hallmark of a single displacement reaction. The other options describe no reaction, gas evolution (not relevant here), or a simple temperature change without displacement.
